chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man performs circuits around the House, then complains (of a need or illness), he should repeat the Tawaf, meaning the obligatory one.
ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if they have to interrupt their Tawaf due to illness or a personal need?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that if a pilgrim’s Tawaf is interrupted or compromised by illness or a pressing need before completion, the obligatory Tawaf must be repeated to ensure validity. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the completeness (kamal) of ritual acts, distinguishing between mere physical presence and the requisite devotion (khushu) required for the validity of the fard. It reflects the broader principle that physical impediments do not invalidate the act but require its renewal to meet the spiritual and legal standards of the Hajj.
